label: soundness-checked, PROTOTYPE, PENDING CRYPTO AUDIT
scope: Fresh attack-surface review beyond the explicit Phase 4 list and prior app-layer attacks.

findings.name: pepper-rotation duplicate bypass window
findings.evidence: Executed same BL-CLAIM-0001 derivation with BL_DUPLICATE_CHECK_PEPPER=pepper_epoch_A and pepper_epoch_B. The duplicate_check_key and duplicate_nullifier differed; keys_equal=false and nullifiers_equal=false.
findings.why_it_matters: If production rotates the duplicate pepper without checking historical pepper epochs or migrating the nullifier set, the same claim can derive a fresh nullifier and bypass duplicate prevention.
findings.real_now_fixable: Yes: add pepper epoch/version to ruleset governance, keep historical epochs live for duplicate checks, and require migration/audit before retiring an epoch.

findings.name: proof-to-claim-root binding gap
findings.evidence: The new multi-claim circuit public values are rootBefore, rootAfter, batchNullifierCommitment. Current BatchClaimsRegistry batchInputs are claimRoot, resultRoot, nullifierRootBefore, nullifierRootAfter, paymentRoot, rulesetRoot, verifierKeyId. No current contract field binds batchNullifierCommitment to claim/result/payment roots.
findings.why_it_matters: A valid nullifier transition proof alone does not prove that the claimRoot/resultRoot/paymentRoot correspond to those exact nullifiers. A production adapter must bind the nullifier commitment into the claim/result leaf construction or into on-chain public inputs.
findings.real_now_fixable: Yes: add batchNullifierCommitment to BatchSubmission and batchInputs, and make claim/result leaves include the exact duplicate nullifier committed by the circuit.

findings.name: verifier-key mismatch
findings.evidence: Executed snarkjs verify with N4 proof under N8 verification key and N8 proof under N4 verification key. Both returned Invalid proof.
findings.why_it_matters: This blocks a direct wrong-circuit proof replay. The contract still needs strict verifierKeyId-to-vkey governance for the eventual on-chain adapter.
findings.real_now_fixable: Already blocked at proof-system level; still needs adapter governance tests when wired.

findings.name: public-input trailing data ambiguity
findings.evidence: BatchClaimsRegistry._batchInputsMatch currently checks batchInputs.length >= 7, not == 7. Extra trailing public inputs are ignored by registry matching.
findings.why_it_matters: Once a real verifier adapter is added, loose length checks can create ambiguity between what the registry stores and what the verifier actually verifies.
findings.real_now_fixable: Yes: require exact public input length per verifierKeyId and reject trailing data.

findings.name: trusted setup file scale and provenance
findings.evidence: N4 used pot19_final.ptau; N8 used pot20_final.ptau. These were locally generated prototype ceremony files, not production MPC/beacon artifacts.
findings.why_it_matters: Groth16 soundness depends on setup toxic-waste disposal. Prototype setup is not acceptable for production.
findings.real_now_fixable: Careful track: replace with audited ceremony/beacon or move to a transparent proof system.
